evidence_policy: Passages read from primary-source HTML; quotations are short excerpts. Local proposals and arithmetic are not published Jeff results.

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
sources.method_data_model_scale: Temperature-softened class-probability distillation mixed with hard labels. MNIST: 60,000 cases, two-hidden-layer 1,200-unit teacher and 800-unit student. Speech: about 85M parameter networks, 10-model ensemble, about 2,000 hours/700M frames.

claims.claim: Soft targets can encode relationships between wrong classes and support sample-efficient transfer.
claims.locator: Section 1, paragraph beginning An obvious way
claims.passage: When the soft targets have high entropy, they provide much more information per training case than hard targets
claims.limits: Conditional mechanism and published fixed-class experiments, not a guarantee with 2–6 dynamic options or teacher mistakes.

claims.claim: Use same temperature for teacher and student; compensate soft-loss scale with T squared when combining losses.
claims.passage: The same high temperature is used when training the distilled model
claims.additional_passage: it is important to multiply them by T² when using both hard and soft targets
claims.limits: Not evidence that any chosen T or mixing weight is optimal for Jeff; no calibration result.

claims.claim: Logit matching equivalence needs centered logits; limited student capacity can favor intermediate temperatures.
claims.passage: provided the logits are zero-meaned separately for each transfer case
claims.additional_passage: when the distilled model is much too small to capture all of the knowledege in the cumbersome model, intermediate temperatures work best
claims.limits: High-temperature approximation, fixed class spaces. Hidden-state or vocabulary matching across Qwen and MiniLM is not established.

claims.claim: MNIST distilled small model reduces reported test errors from 146 to 74, versus teacher 67.
claims.limits: Different domain and scales. Other missing-class illustrations tune bias on test performance and should not be copied as a held-out methodology.

sources.title: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes
sources.method_data_model_scale: Separate label-generation and rationale-generation tasks with prefixes. PaLM 540B teacher; T5 220M data-efficiency experiments and 220M/770M/11B scale experiments; e-SNLI, ANLI, CommonsenseQA, SVAMP. GPT-NeoX 20B teacher ablation.

claims.claim: Studied rationale gains rely on auxiliary generation in training, but rationale generation need not be performed at deployment.
claims.locator: Section 3.2, Multi-task learning with rationales, equations 3–4
claims.passage: instead of using rationales as additional model inputs, we frame learning with rationales as a multi-task problem
claims.additional_passage: the rationale ... is not required in the test time
claims.limits: Not a scalar-encoder auxiliary task; does not show adding rationale text to TRAIN input and dropping it at inference works.

claims.claim: A 220M T5 using 12.5 percent of e-SNLI outperforms standard finetuning using the full source dataset.
claims.passage: by using only 12.5% of the full e-SNLI dataset
claims.limits: A percentage of a benchmark dataset, not proof of gains on 1,500 Jeff decisions. HTML duplicates inline math in extraction; percentages are normalized in this ledger.

claims.claim: Rationale-label concatenation can be harmful relative to label-only finetuning.
claims.locator: Section 4.4, Multi-task training is much more effective than single-task rationale and label joint prediction
claims.passage: single-task training with LLM-rationales can at times leads to worse performance than standard finetuning, e.g., on ANLI and CQA
claims.limits: Specific student/teacher/tasks, not proof all joint CoT finetuning fails.

claims.claim: Teacher quality and task data matter; smaller GPT-NeoX teacher gives smaller lifts, and SVAMP gap required extra unlabeled examples in the reported setup.
claims.locator: Section 4.4 teacher-size ablation; Section 4.2 unlabeled data augmentation
claims.passage: the performance lift is smaller when rationales are extracted from the 20B GPT-NeoX model
claims.additional_passage: ASDiv dataset contains a total of 2,305 examples
claims.limits: Qwen0.5B is much smaller than even this teacher ablation. SVAMP result used 11B student; no 22M generative evidence.

official_implementation.claim: Official implementation distinguishes ground-truth and LLM labels, and task-prefix multitask from standard training.
official_implementation.limits: README inspected, no code run or dependency adopted. Alpha 0.5 is their recommendation, not a Jeff optimum. Main branch is unpinned.

sources.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Multiple Choice Question Answering
sources.method_data_model_scale: Jointly present choices and score answer symbols. Symbol-binding evaluation uses 100 OpenBookQA cases/all 24 orders; models span 1.5B GPT-2 to 178B Jurassic-1. Codex/Davinci broad evaluation covers 20 datasets; exact Codex size not established here.

claims.claim: Answer-symbol scoring is a reasonable decoder decision interface, avoids variable answer-text likelihood normalization, but is only a proxy for correctness probability.
claims.locator: Section 3, Cloze vs. Multiple Choice Prompting
claims.passage: The probabilities of these symbols therefore serve as a proxy for each answer's probability
claims.limits: Requires actual symbol binding; no Qwen0.5B evidence or calibration guarantee. Conditional allowed-symbol normalization is distinct from full-vocabulary mass.

claims.claim: Multiple-choice-symbol binding differs strongly across models and invariance need not imply accuracy.
claims.locator: Section 4, Challenge of Multiple Choice Symbol Binding
claims.passage: PPA measures order invariance irrespective of model ability to perform a task
claims.additional_passage: GPT-2, CodeParrot, and Instruct (Curie) all have PPA scores close to the 25% baseline
claims.limits: Historical checkpoints, 100-case subset. Not proof of Qwen failure. Exhaustive permutations are costly and not a new task recommendation.

claims.claim: Prompt scoring superiority is model dependent rather than universal.
claims.passage: choosing answer options based on cloze prompts ... performs best for GPT-3, MCP always performs best for Instruct and Codex
claims.limits: Three-task direct comparison; wider 20-task evidence uses selected Codex. Does not establish decoder architecture superiority over Jeff's fine-tuned encoder.

official_implementation.claim: Official code resource fetched as an auxiliary cross-reference.
official_implementation.limits: No material algorithmic claim rests on this README; no implementation executed. Main branch unpinned.

sources.title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
sources.method_data_model_scale: Instruction tuning on 62 NLP datasets with held-out task clusters; main 137B language model; scale ablation 422M, 2B, 8B, 68B, 137B.

claims.claim: Instruction tuning can hurt unseen-task performance at smaller scales in an early FLAN recipe.
claims.passage: for the 8B and smaller models ... instruction tuning actually hurts performance on held-out tasks
claims.limits: Capacity explanation is speculative; S5 gives counterevidence with other recipes. Do not infer a universal 8B cutoff or inability of small pretrained models to learn instructions.

claims.claim: Broad instruction tuning here is far outside a one-run local intervention.
claims.passage: This instruction tuning takes around 60 hours on a TPUv3 with 128 cores
claims.limits: Historical 137B experiment cost, not a laptop estimate or requirement for all instruction tuning.

sources.title: Designing Data and Methods for Effective Instruction Tuning (Flan Collection)
sources.method_data_model_scale: Most ablations T5-XL 3B; scaling spans T5 Small/Base/Large/XL/XXL and task counts 8,25,50,100,200,400,800,all 1873. Text also says 1836; source inconsistency preserved. Held-in QA/NLI, CoT, held-out MMLU and BBH.

claims.claim: Later instruction recipes show gains at smaller T5 scales, so the early FLAN result is not a universal small-model prohibition.
claims.locator: Section 3.3, Scaling Small Models to 1.8k+ Tasks
claims.passage: both Held-In and Held-Out tasks appear to benefit from adding hundreds of finetuning tasks
claims.additional_passage: only T5-Small appears to exceed its Held-Out task performance before 1836 tasks
claims.limits: Not 22M MiniLM or 1,500-example Jeff evidence. Held-in performance peaks around 200 tasks then can fall; diversity/quality matter.

claims.claim: Source mixture balancing matters in an instruction-tuning setting and motivates a controlled exposure-weighting hypothesis, not a known Jeff cure.
claims.passage: the mixture weighting deserves as much attention to optimize results
claims.numerical_locator: Table 1: MMLU zero-shot 50.3 full model versus 45.4 without mixture balancing
claims.limits: 3B T5 study; weights chosen partly with practitioner intuition. Equal-source weighting of Jeff's correlated/noisy sources could hurt; no guarantee of independent-rule transfer.

unsupported_equivalences_rejected: Verbal confidence or generated probability JSON equals true token/option probabilities
Teacher agreement equals independently verified truth
Published small generative student equals 22M scalar encoder
Rationale distillation gains require generating rationales at deployment
Rationale distillation gains demonstrate scalar-only supervision can absorb the same procedures
Qwen0.5B comparison outcomes or teacher qualification are already known
scope_exclusions: No raw Evaluation, probe, final, or TRAIN rows inspected
No tracked edits, merges, commits, or mailbox posts
